t:
(a) In General.—
        (1) Scope.—The scope of the construction under this section shall be as generally described in the document entitled “Blackfeet Water Storage, Development, and Project Report”, prepared by DOWL HKM, and dated March 13, 2013, as modified and agreed to by the Secretary and the Tribe. 
        (2) Modification.—The Tribe may modify the scope of the projects described in the document referred to in paragraph (1) if—
            (A) the modified project is—
                (i) similar to the proposed project; and 
                (ii) consistent with the purposes of this subtitle; and  
            (B) the modification is approved by the Secretary.   
    (b) Nonreimbursability of Costs.—All costs incurred by the Secretary in carrying out this section shall be nonreimbursable. 
    (c) Funding.—The total amount of obligations incurred by the Secretary in carrying out this section, prior to any adjustment provided for in section 3718, shall not exceed $91,000,000. 
    (d) OM&R Costs.—The Federal Government shall have no obligation to pay for the OM&R costs for the facilities rehabilitated or constructed under this section. 
    (e) Ownership by Tribe.—Title to any facility constructed under this section shall be held by the Tribe.

fable.w: The scope of federally funded construction carried out by the Secretary is set by agreement between the Secretary and the Tribe, and the Tribe may modify the project scope subject to the Secretary's approval. That brings a party outside the federal government into a federal decision. The tempting contrary reading is that this is only a past agreement or an application-style approval, but the text makes the Tribe's agreement and proposed modifications part of defining what the Secretary builds.
fable.s: as modified and agreed to by the Secretary and the Tribe

qwen_block.w: The section requires that the scope of the federal construction project be 'agreed to by the Secretary and the Tribe.' This establishes a mandatory coordination and agreement process with an outside entity (the Tribe) before the federal government proceeds with the decision to construct the project. This fits the definition of participation as it involves consulting/coordinating with a non-federal party before making a decision.
qwen_block.s: The scope of the construction under this section shall be as generally described in the document entitled “Blackfeet Water Storage, Development, and Project Report”, prepared by DOWL HKM, and dated March 13, 2013, as modified and agreed to by the Secretary and the Tribe.

opus.w: The scope of construction the Secretary carries out must be agreed to by both the Secretary and the Blackfeet Tribe. The Tribe is outside the federal government, so this is coordination with an outside party on a federal decision. One could read the Tribe's later modifications as applications for the Secretary's approval, which would not count. But the requirement that the Tribe agree to the scope in the first place makes the Tribe a party to the decision, not just an applicant for benefits.
opus.s: as modified and agreed to by the Secretary and the Tribe.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is "No." Paragraph (a)(2) can look like an application: the Tribe proposes a change and the Secretary approves it, much like a grantee asking permission. Ownership and cost terms also look like simple funding rules. But paragraph (a)(1) goes further. The Secretary carries out the construction, and its scope is set by a document "as modified and agreed to by the Secretary and the Tribe." So the federal decision about what to build is made jointly with an Indian tribe, which is outside the federal government. That is coordination with an outside party before federal action.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the process for a Tribe to modify a project scope for federal construction funding, which requires Secretary approval. This is an application for a federal benefit (construction/funding), and the approval process is part of the grant/contract administration, not a participatory consultation process as defined. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants.
qwen_chat.s: (2) Modification.—The Tribe may modify the scope of the projects described in the document referred to in paragraph (1) if— (A) the modified project is— (i) similar to the proposed project; and (ii) consistent with the purposes of this subtitle; and (B) the modification is approved by the Secretary.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the Secretary to approve modifications constitutes "participation" because it involves coordination with the Tribe. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, grants, or contracts. Here, the Tribe is applying for federal funding/construction (a benefit), and the Secretary's approval is part of the administrative review of that application, not a consultation process where the Tribe helps shape a broader federal policy or decision through an advisory role or public comment. The interaction is transactional (approval of a specific project scope for funding) rather than participatory in the sense of the definition (consultation/coordination before a decision involving outside input on the decision-making process itself). The key is that the Tribe is the applicant/beneficiary, and the Secretary is the grantor. This falls under the "applications for benefits" trap.
